t:
That Section 1 of the Act entitled “An Act to authorize the transportation of dependents and household effects of personnel of the Navy, Marine Corps, Coast Guard, and Coast and Geodetic Survey, incident to secret or confidential orders, and for other purposes”, approved October 14, 1942 (56 Stat. 786), as amended, is hereby further amended as follows:

    (a) 
Strike out the words “points to new stations in the United States to which such personnel may be subsequently ordered for duty, under such regulations as the Secretary of the Navy may prescribe: Provided, That the wives of” as they appear in lines 13, 14, and 15 thereof, on page 786, volume 56, Statutes at Large, and insert in lieu thereof the words “points to current or new stations to which such personnel may be subsequently ordered for duty, at which restrictive conditions no longer prevail, under such regulations as the Secretary of the Navy may prescribe, and without regard to cost of transportation previously provided for dependents and household effects to such points: Provided, That the wives of”.
 
    (b) 
Strike out the words “personnel concerned have been so ordered shall constitute authority” as they appear in line 26 thereof, on page 786, volume 56, Statutes at Large, and insert in lieu thereof the words “personnel concerned have been so ordered, or that they have been ordered to new duty stations or continued on current duty stations where their dependents are not restricted from joining them, shall constitute authority”.

fable.w: The amended text authorizes the Secretary of the Navy to prescribe regulations governing transportation of dependents and household effects, and under the definition a grant of rulemaking authority counts as participation even when it is discretionary ("may prescribe"). The tempting reading is that this is purely an internal military benefits provision with no outside party named, but the rulemaking authority is what triggers the label. Confidence is moderate because these are internal military regulations and no comment period, hearing, or outside consultation is expressly required.
fable.s: under such regulations as the Secretary of the Navy may prescribe, and without regard to cost of transportation previously provided for dependents and household effects to such points

qwen_block.w: This section amends a statute regarding the transportation of military dependents. It grants the Secretary of the Navy authority to prescribe regulations for this administrative process. There is no requirement for consultation with outside parties, public comment, or advisory boards involving non-federal members. The decision-making process described is internal to the federal government.
qwen_block.s: under such regulations as the Secretary of the Navy may prescribe

opus.w: The amended text gives the Secretary of the Navy authority to prescribe regulations for these transportation benefits. Following Example 6, a grant of rulemaking authority counts as participation, even when the agency is not required to use it. Reading this as a purely internal military amendment with no outside parties overlooks that convention, though the usual exemption of military personnel rules from public comment makes this a closer call.
opus.s: points to current or new stations to which such personnel may be subsequently ordered for duty, at which restrictive conditions no longer prevail, under such regulations as the Secretary of the Navy may prescribe
opus.b: 1. **Thinking it through.** On a first read this is a technical amendment about moving Navy families' household goods, with no outside parties, hearings or committees. That would point to "No." But the new language Congress inserts keeps the phrase "under such regulations as the Secretary of the Navy may prescribe." Under Example 6, a statute that gives a federal agency authority to issue regulations counts as participation, even when using that authority is optional. The case against "Yes" is that regulations on military personnel are usually exempt from the public comment process. Even so, the labelling convention treats a grant of rulemaking authority as enough, so I lean "Yes" with moderate confidence.

qwen_chat.w: This section amends the eligibility criteria for transportation benefits for military personnel and their dependents. While it mentions that the Secretary may prescribe regulations, it does not require any specific participatory process such as public comment, hearings, or consultation with outside entities. The definition excludes applications for benefits and intra-governmental coordination. The authority to prescribe regulations alone, without a mandated participatory mechanism, does not constitute participation under the provided definition.
qwen_chat.s: under such regulations as the Secretary of the Navy may prescribe
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the phrase "under such regulations as the Secretary of the Navy may prescribe" implies a rulemaking process that could involve public participation. However, the definition explicitly states that the mere authority to issue regulations is not sufficient on its own unless the text *requires* a specific participatory mechanism (like a comment period or hearing). Furthermore, this section is primarily about amending eligibility criteria for transportation benefits for military dependents, which falls under the "applications for benefits" trap or simply internal administrative regulation. There is no mention of consulting with outsiders, holding public hearings, or creating advisory boards with non-federal members. The decision-making process described is entirely internal to the Department of the Navy.
